BiblicalUsage: Twice, the small adverb that counts, from the Pharisee who fasted twice in the week to the cock that would crow twice before Peter denied Jesus. Paul was hindered once and again from coming to the Thessalonians, and Jude's twice-dead trees bear no fruit at all.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God counts what I repeat, whether it is fasting, failure, or fruitlessness. Twice can be a boast, a warning, or a sorrow, and I want my twice to be the kind that bears fruit.
